splash_label.note: A screen reader's name for the opening screen that shows the studio's mark. Two or three words at most; it is never drawn.

splash_hint.note: Blinks under the studio's mark on the opening screen. Tells the player that pressing any key or tapping the screen goes on.

menu_title.note: The game's name, the big title on the main menu. A proper name: keep it as it is, in the Latin letters.

menu_hint.note: One line under the title that says what the game is about. The player is a small hooded figure carrying a lantern up through ruins to a glowing ember. Warm and short.

play.note: The big button on the main menu that starts the game.

keys_move.note: On the main menu, after the arrow keys: 'left and right arrows move'. One lower-case verb, followed on screen by the next key's name.

keys_jump.note: On the main menu, after the Space key: 'Space jumps'. One lower-case verb.

keys_pause.note: On the main menu, after the Esc key: 'Esc pauses'. One lower-case verb.

pause.note: The name of the small pause button in the corner while playing, read by screen readers; the button shows only two bars. The word for stopping the game for a moment.

paused_title.note: Heading of the screen that shows while the game is paused: the game is stopped, nothing is lost.

resume.note: The big button on the paused screen that carries on playing.

back_to_menu.note: A button on the paused screen that leaves the round and goes back to the main menu.

end_title.note: Heading when the player reaches the ember and wins. A short, warm line of congratulation.

play_again.note: The big button on the win screen that starts another round.

menu.note: A button on the win screen that goes back to the main menu. One short word.

end_time.note: How long the climb took. {seconds} is a number such as 12.34, already written for the player's language. Keep the unit short: seconds.
